subject: How to fix some parameters in multi-state models with fixed group effects

messages.author: ae0d0faac04406b4
messages.subject: How to fix some parameters in multi-state models with fixed group effects
parts:
Dear all,

I am currently working on a multi-state known fate model to investigate cause-specific mortality (hunting and other sources of mortality).
I was able to write and to run such a model in my situation with 3 differents sites (no dispersion) and with 2 groups (wild or released individuals).
I reduced the time effect to a seasonal effect using a covariate for each occasion.
The model is able to estimate quite well all parameters. However, there is no hunting for 2 sites, and the hunting mortality is estimated in the range: 0.00-0.10, not clearly 0 ...
Therefore, I would like to fix the hunting mortality to 0 for these 2 sites to avoid some bias in the estimation.

I tried to define separately the a[,,,] fixed to 0 and those that will be estimated but it doesn't work.

If you have some tricks, they are welcome !

Thanks for the help.
Best wishes,

Guillaume

here is the current working code:

# Import dataset
data <- read.table("PR_real.txt",header=F,sep="\t")
colnames(data) <- c(seq(1,92,1),"sexe","Mage","Origin","site")
n.ind <- dim(data)[1]
## creater vectors to collect information on origin, site, sex
origin <- c(rep(NA,n.ind))
site <- as.numeric(data[,"site"])
sex <- as.numeric(data[,"sexe"])
for (i in 1:n.ind){
  or <- as.numeric(data[,"Origin"]) # 2 levels: R & W => R=1 & W=2
  if (or[i]==1){ # if bird is a released bird
    origin[i] <- 2
  } else {
    origin[i] <- 1
  }
}
origin
site
sex

## create matrix with capture histories only
CH <- matrix(as.matrix(data[,1:92]),ncol=ncol(data[,1:92]),dimnames=NULL)
head(CH)

## create vector to categorize the season
# marking began in April, thus first month in study = April
# year = 5 months of "Breeding", 3 months of "Hunting" and 4 months of "Other"
n.years <- dim(CH)[2]%/%12 # number of complete years on the data set
left <- dim(CH)[2]%%12  # number of left months
season <- c(rep(c(rep(1,5),rep(2,3),rep(3,4)),n.years),c(rep(1,5),rep(2,3)))

# Create vector with occasion of marking 
get.first <- function(x) min(which(x!=0))
f <- apply(CH, 1, get.first)

# Recode CH matrix: note, a 0 is not allowed!
# 1 = alive, 2 = recovered Hunted, 3 = recovered Dead, 4 = not detected
rMR <- CH  # Recoded CH
rMR[rMR==0] <- 4

# Specify model in BUGS language
sink("msmr.bug")
cat("
    model {
    
    # -------------------------------------------------
    # Parameters:
    # mH=m[1]         Hunting mortality probability
    # mN=m[2]         Natural mortality probability
    # m[3]=1-sum(m[]) survival prob
    # l:              loss of signal from radiotracking device
    # -------------------------------------------------
    # States (S):
    # 1 alive and active transmitter
    # 2 alive but inactive transmitter (not observable)
    # 3 recently dead and recovered hunted
    # 4 recently dead and recovered
    # 5 Dead (absorbing, not observable)
    # Observations (O):
    # 1 detected alive
    # 2 recovered Hunted
    # 3 recovered dead
    # 4 not detected
    # -------------------------------------------------
    
    ## Priors and constraints
    # Prior for loss of signal
    for (t in 1:(n.occasions-1)){
      l[t]  <- l.seas[season[t]]
    }
    for (s in 1:3){
      l.seas[s] ~ dunif(0,1)
    }
    
    # fixed time and groups effect for survival and cause-specific mortality
    for (i in 1:nind){ #ind      
      for (t in 1:(n.occasions-1)){ #time -> season
        for (b in 1:3){ # which parameters 1=mH,2=mN,3=S
          m[b,t,i,i] <- m.comp[b,season[t],site[i],origin[i]]
        }
      }
    }
    # dirichlet prior for mortality and survival
    for (b in 1:3){ #param              1=mH,2=mN,3=S
      for (t in 1:3){ #season           1=Breed,2=Hunt,3=Other
        for (s in 1:3){ #site              1=Lu,2=Pa,3=Po
          for (k in 1:2){ #origin         1=W,2=R
            a[b,t,s,k] ~ dgamma(1,1)
            m.comp[b,t,s,k] <- a[b,t,s,k]/sum(a[,t,s,k])    # m.comp[1,t,1,1] & m.comp[1,t,3,1] should be fixed to 0
          }
        }
      }    
    }
   
    ## Define state-transition and observation matrices   
    for (i in 1:nind){
    # Define probabilities of state S(t+1) given S(t)
    for (t in f[i]:(n.occasions-1)){
    ps[1,i,t,1] <- (1-l[t])*m[3,t,i,i]
    ps[1,i,t,2] <- l[t]
    ps[1,i,t,3] <- (1-l[t])*m[1,t,i,i]
    ps[1,i,t,4] <- (1-l[t])*m[2,t,i,i]
    ps[1,i,t,5] <- 0
    ps[2,i,t,1] <- 0
    ps[2,i,t,2] <- 1
    ps[2,i,t,3] <- 0
    ps[2,i,t,4] <- 0
    ps[2,i,t,5] <- 0
    ps[3,i,t,1] <- 0
    ps[3,i,t,2] <- 0
    ps[3,i,t,3] <- 0
    ps[3,i,t,4] <- 0
    ps[3,i,t,5] <- 1
    ps[4,i,t,1] <- 0
    ps[4,i,t,2] <- 0
    ps[4,i,t,3] <- 0
    ps[4,i,t,4] <- 0
    ps[4,i,t,5] <- 1
    ps[5,i,t,1] <- 0
    ps[5,i,t,2] <- 0
    ps[5,i,t,3] <- 0
    ps[5,i,t,4] <- 0
    ps[5,i,t,5] <- 1
    
    # Define probabilities of O(t) given S(t)
    po[1,i,t,1] <- 1
    po[1,i,t,2] <- 0
    po[1,i,t,3] <- 0
    po[1,i,t,4] <- 0
    po[2,i,t,1] <- 0
    po[2,i,t,2] <- 0
    po[2,i,t,3] <- 0
    po[2,i,t,4] <- 1
    po[3,i,t,1] <- 0
    po[3,i,t,2] <- 1
    po[3,i,t,3] <- 0
    po[3,i,t,4] <- 0
    po[4,i,t,1] <- 0
    po[4,i,t,2] <- 0
    po[4,i,t,3] <- 1
    po[4,i,t,4] <- 0
    po[5,i,t,1] <- 0
    po[5,i,t,2] <- 0
    po[5,i,t,3] <- 0
    po[5,i,t,4] <- 1
    } #t
    } #i
    
    # Likelihood 
    for (i in 1:nind){
    # Define latent state at first capture   # all individuals are captured as alive and active radiotracker => 1
    z[i,f[i]] <- 1
    for (t in (f[i]+1):n.occasions){
    # State process: draw S(t) given S(t-1)
    z[i,t] ~ dcat(ps[z[i,t-1], i, t-1,])
    # Observation process: draw O(t) given S(t)
    y[i,t] ~ dcat(po[z[i,t], i, t-1,])
    } #t
    } #i
    }
    ",fill = TRUE)
sink()

parts:
Dear Guillaume,

 

I think that you need to fix m.comp directly to zero and to remove those bits from the loop where the multinomial logit link function is defined. Hence, try this:
for (t in 1:3){ #season           1=Breed,2=Hunt,3=Other

m.comp[1,t,1,1] <- 0

   m.comp[1,t,2,1] <- 1

   m.comp[1,t,3,1] <- 0

   }

  

    for (b in 2:3){ #param              1=mH,2=mN,3=S

for (t in 1:3){ #season           1=Breed,2=Hunt,3=Other

        for (s in 1:3){ #site              1=Lu,2=Pa,3=Po

          for (k in 1:2){ #origin         1=W,2=R

            a[b,t,s,k] ~ dgamma(1,1)

m.comp[b,t,s,k] <- a[b,t,s,k]/sum(a[2:3,t,s,k])    # m.comp[1,t,1,1] & m.comp[1,t,3,1] should be fixed to 0

          }

        }

      }   

    }

 

Kind regards

 

Michael

season <- c(rep(c(rep(1,5),rep(2,3),rep(3,4)),n.years),c(rep(1,5),rep(2,3)))

cat("

    model {

    ## Priors and constraints

    # Prior for loss of signal

    for (t in 1:(n.occasions-1)){

      l[t]  <- l.seas[season[t]]

    }

    for (s in 1:3){

      l.seas[s] ~ dunif(0,1)

    }

    

    # fixed time and groups effect for survival and cause-specific mortality

    ps[1,i,t,4] <- (1-l[t])*m[2,t,i,i]

    ps[1,i,t,5] <- 0

    ps[2,i,t,1] <- 0

    ps[2,i,t,2] <- 1

    ps[2,i,t,3] <- 0

    ps[3,i,t,1] <- 0

    } #i

parts:
Dear Michi,

Thanks for the tips.
After several trials to fix m.comp outside the loop, it finally worked for my study case (no hunting mortality [mH] for wild birds in 2 sites, no released birds on those 2 sites, no mH for 2 seasons on the 3rd site for both wild and released birds).
Now only real parameters are estimated.

Thanks.

Best regards,
Guillaume

Here is the final code:

    # 3 recovered dead

    for (t in 1:(n.occasions-1)){
      l[t]  <- l.seas[season[t]]
    }
    for (s in 1:3){
      l.seas[s] ~ dunif(0,1)
    }
## overall dirichlet prior for mortality and survival

for (i in 1:nind){ #ind      
      for (t in 1:(n.occasions-1)){ #time -> season
        for (b in 1:3){ # which parameters

m[b,t,i,i] <- m.comp[b,season[t],site[i],origin[i]]

## Individuals in Luberon and Porquerolles
    # fixing values for wild ind
for (t in 1:3){

for (s in 2:3){

    # fixing values for released ind
for (t in 1:3){
for (b in 1:3){

      }

    # priors for parameters to be estimated
for (b in 2:3){ #param
for (t in 1:3){ #season

for (s in 2:3){ #site only Lu(2) and Po(3)
          a[b,t,s,1] ~ dgamma(1,1)
          m.comp[b,t,s,1] <- a[b,t,s,1]/sum(a[2:3,t,s,1])

    ## Individuals in Pailhès

for (k in 1:2){

m.comp[1,t,1,k] <- 0

    # priors for parameters (mH,mN,S) for hunting season in Pailhès
for (b in 1:3){ #param
for (k in 1:2){ #origin

a[b,1,1,k] ~ dgamma(1,1)

for (b in 2:3){ #param
for (t in 2:3){ #season
for (k in 1:2){ #origin

a[b,t,1,k] ~ dgamma(1,1)

Betreff: How to fix some parameters in multi-state models with fixed group effects

 

Dear all,

 

I am currently working on a multi-state known fate model to investigate cause-specific mortality (hunting and other sources of mortality).

I was able to write and to run such a model in my situation with 3 differents sites (no dispersion) and with 2 groups (wild or released individuals).

I reduced the time effect to a seasonal effect using a covariate for each occasion.

The model is able to estimate quite well all parameters. However, there is no hunting for 2 sites, and the hunting mortality is estimated in the range: 0.00-0.10, not clearly 0 ...

Therefore, I would like to fix the hunting mortality to 0 for these 2 sites to avoid some bias in the estimation.

 

I tried to define separately the a[,,,] fixed to 0 and those that will be estimated but it doesn't work.

 

If you have some tricks, they are welcome !

 

Thanks for the help.

Best wishes,

 

Guillaume
